titleEn: Even in the Dark, the Shop Light Shines!

pages.text: "Tonight I will walk home myself!" Nono, the smallest, roundest sparrow, stood tall. Grandpa lowered the shop awning. Awning down meant bedtime.
Alley lamps came on. Kiki, the pointy-eared cat, and Gugu, the broad-chested pigeon, waved and went home. But the lamp outside Nono's home was out. That spot was dark.
Nono stopped. Something pointed swayed above the dark wall. "Wh-what is that?" He gripped his scarf.
The shop door creaked open. Grandpa Badger came out with a lantern. "You were scared. Come look over there." Nono turned toward his hand.
Grandpa pointed down the dark alley. Far away, the shop window glowed round and bright. "Even in the dark, the shop light shines! I leave it on all night."
Grandpa shone the lantern on the dark wall. "If it scares you, look again." Nono looked at the pointed shadow. A snow shovel hanging under the roof edge! "No monster!" He giggled.
Nono walked through the dark alley step by step. Kiki waved from the wall, Gugu from the window. Nono waved too. "Even in the dark, the shop light shines!"
Nono slipped into his home beneath the roof edge. He touched his green scarf and looked out. At the alley end, the shop light glowed.
Now he was not afraid of night. "One, say you are scared! Two, find the shop light! Three, look again at what scares you!" He pulled the blanket to his neck.
In the morning, Grandpa lifted Nono in both hands for a hug. Even in darkness, one shop light stayed on all night. Nono hopped. "Even in the dark, the shop light shines!"
